answer: A near-duplicate is rejected at the pigment gate and the submitting identity is flagged, so one good text cannot be reused across aliases. Copying an answer therefore yields nothing, and producing 81 genuinely distinct answers per epoch is real inference work with real latency; the beacon ledger keeps the similarity graph, and the vault review can re-run it. Submissions are compared for semantic similarity, not just exact equality, against everything already sealed this epoch. That is 5 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
